page.text: Being a modern library, NTgCalls requires CMake 3.27+ and Python 3.10+ to be built on your system. On Linux it also needs libasound2 and libpulse-dev. We recommend using the latest version of CMake.
page.alert: Before building NTgCalls, check for pre-compiled shared libs on GitHub Releases, Python bindings on PyPI, the Node.js package on npm or the crate on crates.io. Building from source may be necessary if pre-compiled packages are not available.
On Linux x86_64, macOS and Android the build downloads its own Clang toolchain, so there is nothing to install by hand. Linux ARM64 is the only platform that uses the system compiler.
page.text: Below, we will guide you through the step-by-step process of installing the prerequisites required to compile NTgCalls on your operating system.

subtext.text: Every binding is built through the same entry point, setup.py build_lib, which takes the target you want and reads how to build it from that target's own configuration. Run every command from the root directory of the project.
subtext.alert: It's essential to have Python 3.10+ installed on your system.

subtext.text: For developers looking to use NTgCalls with C and C++, we provide C bindings. This is the default target, so it needs no --target:
The libraries and the generated ntgcalls.h are written to shared-output or static-output.
The Python bindings are installed like any other package, and the extension is compiled as part of the install:
The Node.js addon is built through the same command, and lands in targets/node/build/Release:
The crate links against the C shared library. Build it once, then point the crate at the result through NTGCALLS_LIB_DIR, otherwise the build script downloads the matching release from GitHub:
subtext.syntax-highlight: $ python3 setup.py build_lib --static $ NTGCALLS_LIB_DIR=$PWD/static-output/lib cargo build --manifest-path targets/rust/Cargo.toml

subtext.text: build_lib also accepts --no-preserve-cache to drop the build directory once it is done, and --defines=key=value;key2=value2 to override any substitution the target configuration uses.

Two more commands are available: list_targets prints the targets that can be built, and generate writes the language-agnostic schema every binding and the documentation are generated from, without building anything.
subtext.syntax-highlight: $ python3 setup.py list_targets $ python3 setup.py generate
